original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: Search the 143 adjacent call pairs in the pinned selected #1094 GLOBAL-TEMPLATE execution schedule for a same-orientation direct eight-row centre-source owner/chart boundary with disjoint complete 112-row target panels, sufficient to instantiate the PR1708/1748 two-panel interface without added owner transport.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks whether consecutive calls can eliminate reconstructed work. PR1708 and PR1748 supplied the local shared-centre maps, while PR1791 priced the actual-profile headroom. This refined experiment tests the remaining direct-owner witness in the selected schedule; it does not repeat the local algebra or budget derivation.
bottleneck_link: A direct shared centre boundary could save 32 paid-mass units per call, but the remaining actual-profile budget is below 32 and any owner, chart, precision, frame, restoration, hosting, or interface cost must fit inside it.
stop_rule: Decode exactly the 144 calls and test all 143 adjacent ordered pairs. Stop after the census. Do not widen to nonadjacent calls or changed schedules; do not claim alias or transport impossibility.
evidence: The exact verifier binds all 144 calls to local sweep events and pinned forward/backward program digests; reconstructs all 8 centre source roles and all 22 targets per centre from each orientation; confirms both target lists against the canonical cut; checks complete 112-row target owner panels; and tests all 143 adjacent pairs. Result: 81 same-orientation, 62 mixed; all 81 same-orientation panels disjoint; zero common physical centre-source owners in all 81; 9 with all charts equal but owners still distinct; zero directly eligible pairs. Six synthetic controls pass. Reproduce with python3 -I -O -B research/selected-centre-adjacent-pair-seed01fcb1/verify.py.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in source inspection, exact census construction, verifier implementation, and packaging.

open_questions.question: Can a nonadjacent same-orientation pair in the selected schedule share the direct eight-row owner/chart boundary while its full target panels are disjoint?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Such a pair could expose a reusable centre interface if intervening operations preserve the source rows and the changed schedule composition remains legal.
open_questions.first_step: Index the same pinned 144 owner maps by exact eight-row source signature and target-panel signature, then inspect only repeated signatures for intervening execution events.
open_questions.blocked_by: The current experiment intentionally stops at adjacent pairs. Even a matching endpoint pair would need a proof that intervening calls and frame changes preserve the boundary, plus a full overhead invoice.
